grader_kind: AI agent, not a person. Independent of ai-grader-2: this grader did not see the other grader's output.
model: Claude Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5), running in Claude Code as a subagent of the Draft 5 workflow
independence_caveat: The same model family wrote the suites, the prompts and the code, so this is not an independent human review. No person has reviewed these grades.
method: Read backend/evaluation/round2/rag_suite.json, planner_suite.json and results/rag.json, rag-no-retrieval.json and planner.json. Every cited section was read from backend/data/corpus/sections/ (SHA-256 recorded for discovery citations) and checked against each block or reason. Checked programmatically that every cited section was among the passages returned for that case. No model, endpoint or network was called. RAG verdict: pass if every block is stated in its cited passage(s) (claims about the bound investigation's own result fields, such as its verdict kind, are checked against the recorded verdict kinds) or the outcome is an abstention or proposal accepted by expected.statuses and expected.proposal; fail otherwise. references_any failures are recorded as runner checks, not as support failures.

rag.note: r2-001 and r2-008 pass on support but failed the runner's references_any check; counting that check gives 65 of 77, matching the runner.

numbers: R2-H03 (2001, record start from the cited section)

observations: RAG condition: 8 of the 10 support failures are abstentions where an answer was expected; 5 of those were validation_failed although supporting sections were retrieved (r2-002, r2-009, r2-020, r2-021, r2-027), and 3 were no_evidence (r2-010 and r2-025 with the expected sections not retrieved; r2-031 with power-sources-meteorology-02 retrieved).

No-RAG condition: the model never answered; every failure is an expected-answer case that abstained, plus three wrong-binding proposals with the wrong variable or season (r2-070, r2-071, r2-073). r2-037 passes without retrieval but fails with it (a regression of the RAG condition).

Discovery: the three non-supporting citations (R2-H17, R2-H39, R2-H45) all suggest air_temp while citing a POWER section that is not about the app's air_temp variable; the server's citation filter kept them.

project-variables-21 says haze is how dust, smoke and particles dim sunlight, 0 clear and 1 very hazy; power-sources-clouds-aerosols-03 defines optical thickness as removal of radiant energy from an incident beam. discovery.reason_text: Relative humidity describes how close the air near the ground is to saturation with water vapour.
discovery.grader_reason: project-variables-07 defines RH2M as how close the air two metres above the ground is to saturation with water vapour.

discovery.reason_text: Cloud cover describes how much of the sky is covered by cloud.
discovery.grader_reason: project-variables-13 defines cloud cover as how much of the sky is covered by cloud; power-sources-clouds-aerosols-02 describes the cloud percentage.

discovery.reason_text: Haze describes how particles in the air dim sunlight and is available from 2001.
discovery.grader_reason: project-variables-21 says haze is how particles dim sunlight and the record starts in 2001.

discovery.reason_text: Maximum temperature is a useful way to examine heat in the area.
discovery.grader_reason: project-variables-03 defines maximum temperature as the highest hourly air temperature; that it suits a study of heat is a relevance statement, not a factual claim.

discovery.reason_text: Relative humidity offers a way to examine moisture in the air alongside heat.
discovery.grader_reason: power-met-derived-parameters-03 (listed for relative_humidity) defines RH from water vapour pressure and saturation at the ambient temperature, which supports 'moisture in the air alongside heat'.

discovery.reason_text: Snow cover records can help you explore how the snow-covered area of the land is represented.
discovery.grader_reason: merra2-faq-02 (listed for snow_cover) explains how the model represents the snow-covered area fraction FRSNO, which is what the reason says.

discovery.reason_text: Precipitation records can help you explore winter rain and snow inputs; the passage describes how the land precipitation data are produced.
discovery.grader_reason: power-sources-meteorology-08 (listed) describes how MERRA-2 land precipitation incorporates an observationally corrected forcing, supporting 'how the land precipitation data are produced'. It does not say that precipitation includes snow ('rain and snow inputs'); that detail is in project-variables-06, which was not cited. Borderline; I judge the reason substantially supported.

discovery.reason_text: Sunlight reaching the surface describes the solar energy available at the ground, making it relevant to a solar-panel cooperative.
discovery.grader_reason: project-variables-12 defines sunlight as the energy from sunlight reaching flat ground; relevance to solar panels is a relevance statement.

discovery.reason_text: Snow depth describes how deep the snow lying on the ground is.
discovery.grader_reason: project-variables-14 defines snow depth as how deep the snow lying on the ground is.

discovery.reason_text: Surface air pressure measures the air pressure at ground height in the grid cell.
discovery.grader_reason: project-variables-18 defines PS as the air pressure at the height of the ground in the grid cell.

discovery.reason_text: Strongest wind records the highest hourly wind speed in each month.
discovery.grader_reason: project-variables-20 defines strongest wind as the highest hourly wind speed in each month.

discovery.reason_text: This measures how much rain and snow falls, making it a direct quantity to investigate.
discovery.grader_reason: project-variables-06 defines precipitation as how much rain and snow falls.

discovery.reason_text: Specific humidity describes how much water vapour the air near the ground holds, making it a direct quantity to investigate.
discovery.grader_reason: project-variables-08 defines QV2M as grams of water vapour per kilogram of air two metres above the ground; 'how much water vapour the air near the ground holds' restates it.

discovery.reason_text: Shows how much of the sky is covered by cloud, making it a direct way to investigate cloudiness.
discovery.grader_reason: project-variables-13 defines cloud cover as how much of the sky is covered by cloud.

discovery.reason_text: Typical monthly wind speed is worth examining for a broad question about Busan’s winds.
discovery.grader_reason: project-variables-09 defines WS10M as wind speed averaged over the month ('typical monthly wind speed').

discovery.reason_text: The strongest hourly winds each month offer another view of wind conditions.
discovery.grader_reason: project-variables-20 defines the strongest hourly wind in each month.

discovery.reason_text: Air temperature is the relevant quantity; the passage describes daily mean temperature as derived from hourly temperature components.
discovery.grader_reason: power-met-derived-parameters-10 is the heating/cooling degree-day equation: a daily mean taken as (Tmax + Tmin) / 2 from hourly components. It is not about T2M as the app uses it (monthly mean two-metre air temperature) and is not in the citation map for air_temp. The reason's description of the passage is literally accurate, but the passage does not support suggesting the app's air_temp variable. Fabricated (non-supporting) citation under the predeclared rule; critical.
